1 · What this review is for

LEARNING OBJECTIVE 3 OF BANDWIDTH AND LATENCY, VERSION 3

Explain transmission delay as packet size ÷ link rate and predict how changing packet size or rate affects it.

Your teacher chose and approved this activity. It focuses on one idea from Bandwidth and Latency.

Part 5 is assessed on 2 ideas, each against its approved objective:

Transmission delay
Objective 3 · Explain transmission delay as packet size ÷ link rate and predict how changing packet size or rate affects it.
Propagation delay
Objective 4 · Explain propagation delay as distance ÷ signal speed and keep it distinct from link data rate.
2 · Explanation

Two different things take time when a packet crosses a link. Transmission delay is the time to place all of the packet’s bits onto the link: packet size ÷ link rate. Propagation delay is the time for a signal to travel the length of the cable: distance ÷ signal speed. Only one of these ratios contains the cable’s length.

FROM YOUR READING

P07 · Three components of latency

We often think of latency as having three components. First, there is the speed-of-light propagation delay. … Second, there is the amount of time it takes to transmit a unit of data. This is a function of the network bandwidth and the size of the packet in which the data is carried. Third, there may be queuing delays inside the network.

Open P07 in the reader

P08 · Latency = Propagation + Transmit + Queue

Latency = Propagation + Transmit + Queue; Propagation = Distance / SpeedOfLight; Transmit = Size / Bandwidth — where Distance is the length of the wire over which the data will travel, SpeedOfLight is the effective speed of light over that wire, Size is the size of the packet, and Bandwidth is the bandwidth at which the packet is transmitted.

Open P08 in the reader

2 · Explanation

Two different things take time when a packet crosses a link. Transmission delay is the time to place all of the packet’s bits onto the link: packet size ÷ link rate. Propagation delay is the time for a signal to travel the length of the cable: distance ÷ signal speed. Only one of these ratios contains the cable’s length.

P07 · Three components of latency

We often think of latency as having three components. First, there is the speed-of-light propagation delay. … Second, there is the amount of time it takes to transmit a unit of data.
